description: Gumbel MCTS chooses the root move by *sequential halving* with Gumbel noise, so it improves the policy even with very few simulations. Each root move gets noise `g`; the search considers the moves with the highest `g + log prior`, spends its simulations on them in rounds, and after each round keeps the better half by `g + log prior + σ(Q)`, where `σ` rescales the Q-values. Below the root, each simulation takes the child whose visit share lags most behind the improved policy `softmax(log prior + σ(Q))`, with no exploration constant. It returns the move that survived the halving and the improved policy, which replaces the visit counts as the training target; a noise scale of 0 makes it deterministic, for evaluating a trained policy. Use it in self-play with a policy network and a small simulation budget, where PUCT with root noise needs many simulations to improve on the prior.

papers.authors: Ivo Danihelka, Arthur Guez, Julian Schrittwieser, David Silver
papers.title: Policy improvement by planning with Gumbel
